Both tests disagree with Table S1 by -16% to -50%; most of these rows have 95% intervals over 30% of the rate and are flagged LOW CONFIDENCE. In those bright early frames the relative threshold locks onto the bright core while a faint blue leading zone extends further upstream. A constant offset does not change a slope, but one that changes over time does. The failures track this bright early phase where the brightness threshold locks onto the flame core.

Consequently, flames and heat dissipation mechanisms that rely on airflow behave in completely unique ways compared to standard terrestrial conditions.

The cross-check ensures that relative speeds between components remain within safe operational limits during critical mission phases.

Engineers realized that passive cooling alone was insufficient to manage extreme lunar temperatures. Consequently, active fan systems remained essential for maintaining safe equipment temperatures on the Moon.

column9: NASA reached this conclusion by analyzing data from combustion experiments conducted in microgravity aboard the International Space Station. Specifically, they used measurements of flame spread rates, temperatures, and gas compositions under different ventilation speeds. These tests revealed that flames continue to burn and spread even when airflow is completely shut off, as heat and oxygen still diffuse through the surrounding area. Therefore, simply turning off the ventilation system is ineffective at extinguishing a fire in reduced gravity environments.
